en: Let us go to form a marriage alliance.
To that fully accomplished, fierce girl
Let us go and place the betrothal earrings.
Pouring out wealth and giving livestock,
Giving whatever wealth and honor are required,
Without dispute or quarrel,
Let us take her according to custom.
Most precious among women,
It is true that she is a skilled craftswoman;
Sacred and most exceptional,
It is true that she is such a girl.
Scattering wealth and giving livestock,
Let us go to Temirkan.
Spreading our hands and saying, 'Amen!'
Let us take Kanykey.”
Thus spoke mighty Bakay,
Making known what they did not know,
Thus setting them upon the right path.
They mounted and rode on again.
If he led, the road was blessed;
If he drove them onward, his troops were countless.
Their elder, old Bakay,
Was a saint wiser than other men.
He finds an eye in darkness,
Finds words at an unexpected moment.
Greathearted Bakay traveled on,
Sparing no horses, covering much ground.
Dusk fell and the sun set;
All the people lay quiet.
The champions rode in high spirits
And came upon the Mediyen desert.
They called it the Mediyen desert:
There was not a pinch of grass to eat,
Not a drop of water on the ground.
The lions Ajybay and Chubak
Had their fill of amusement;
Its lizards flashing,
Darting here and there.
When dawn broke clear,
When light fell upon the earth,
Looking toward the north,
They saw five people emerge on a rise.
Studying their appearance,
When valiant Bakay looked,
The renowned saint
Was Shai Ata himself,
His own dark eyes gazing there.
'I shall give him to my champion,' he said;
The renowned camel, Zhelmaian,
He had brought at that time.
That blessed Zhelmaian
Had reached his fortieth tooth-year.
For Manas, God Most High
Had made him a Buraq.
Making the signs of the task clear,
He had come to set things right.
Shai Ata had come
To support the hero Manas.
That Manas was wolf-maned,
Shai Ata knew.
The dark camel with a broad hump
To Manas himself
He had brought as a gift.
When they saw Shai Ata,
They dismounted then:
Ajybay and their elder Bakay
Stood with hands respectfully folded,
Manas and Chubak, all of them.
Stately Shai Ata,
Standing grandly, stretched out his hand;
Of the leopard-born, bloodstained warrior
He took the hand, standing proudly:
“Oh, my child, youngest of the six lions,
The servant beloved of God,
When anger takes you and you stand erect,
You make blood flow:
You are that very leopard-lion.
Seven years before you were born,
I already knew of you.
'Let me reach him and see his eyes,'
I had been asking God!
Come, my child, give me your hand;
May my God open your road!
Do not turn back from your appointed death;
Do not recoil from dying!
If a sorely pressing turmoil comes,
If a raging uproar comes,
I shall pour forth abundant fire;
Against the shouting enemy
I myself shall support you!
Leopard Manas, bloodstained lion,
You alone were created thus.
To take your hand and see your fair face
I have been wishing;
Zhelmaian, entrusted for you,
I have been wishing to give.
This Zhelmaian standing here,
The dark camel with a broad hump,
Has many sacred powers.
He appears from the unseen,
To a lion like yourself,
To a favored servant he is granted!
This dark camel with a broad hump,
Renowned swift Zhelmaian,
The wind cannot match his trot;
No beast can match his stride.
He skims along flying like a cloud;
The four corners of the round world
He visits in less than four days.
Load sand upon him in saddlebags;
He neither tires of it nor frets.
Know that his power is great.
Such is Zhelmaian's nature:
He is Zhelkaiyp's offspring.
Winged among the beasts,
If you load steel shot upon his back,
Calling it neither light nor heavy,
He is accustomed to carry it.
Zhelmaian is fitting for you,
The swiftest of split-humped camels.
I exchanged shots with the Arabs;
It went beyond measure, my dear child,
The swiftness of Zhelmaian.
Upon his head is a golden halter;
So outstanding are his abilities,
For you, my surpassing lion,
This Zhelmaian is fitting!
Load a great deal of ammunition:
He is a solace to our entrusted lives.
Turn your eyes toward us;
'Shai Ata gave me a gift,' say,
And accept Zhelmaian!
His swiftness and his tireless pace
Make him a helper to all the people.
This Zhelmaian standing here
Knows the four corners of the round world,
The five corners of Mediyen;
He is familiar with them all.
His hump is blunt, his neck thick;
This blessed Zhelmaian
Has strength as a beast of burden too.
If you fight with Kakanchyn,
If you load sacks of steel shot,
He keeps pace with winged steeds;
He has swiftness too.
If you appoint a mount for messages,
To the four corners of the round world,
If you give letters for four circuits,
He can go and deliver them at once:
He has swiftness too.
Both swift and a mighty camel—
My lion, I have known you.
Lion Manas, my wolf-maned one,
'Let him take a faithful companion,'
I have been asking God.
When you say, 'Go!' Zhelmaian
Does not turn his neck like a brute.
If you lash him this way and that
And spur him on either side,
He does not stand bellowing like a camel.
Chewing the tops of birches and willows,
His dark eyes shining,
Esteemed swift Zhelmaian—
If a great, clamorous dispute arises,
If a foe comes firing many shots,
Zhelmaian will be needed.
Into darkly looming Great Beijing,
If you charge straight in and thrust your spear,
With Beijing, that dark destroyer,
If you grapple in combat,
Zhelmaian will give support.
If you take a spear with a black pennon,
If you circle the emperor's outskirts,
Zhelmaian will be of use.
Though the desert is forty days across,
Though a ridge has savage torrents,
He does not weary or thirst.
If you send him running toward the sunrise,
Unless his head is torn off,
He never rests upon the road.
When you give him his head,
This blessed Zhelmaian
Flies and frolics like a cloud.
Though he journeys for months and years,
He does not rest like other beasts.
His swiftness is all the greater;
He takes no daily rest.
Such is his swiftness:
This creature Zhelmaian
Appeared from the unseen.
My wolf-maned one touched by Khizir,
He was found through your good fortune!
Let me tell of Zhelmaian:
From the ridges of Mediyen,
My champion Manas, for you,
From where I went hunting,
In parched deserts,
Where he grew wild in that desert,
From the peoples of the unseen,
We pressed forward in contention,
Fought many days without rest,
And cried in anguish many times to God.
I brought him to you.
Greathearted Manas, my champion,
Dedicating him to you alone,
My champion, I had taken him into my keeping.
'When I meet the wolf-maned one face to face,
I shall give him,' I had said.
It would be shameful if you refused.
Lion-born leopard,
I willingly give this entrusted gift.
He is king among camel-kind.
Youngest of the six lions,
My greathearted one, for you yourself
He is a fitting beast.
Sprawling upon sand, raised in the desert,
Zhelmaian will be a faithful companion.
Ride him on a holy campaign—he will not flinch.
Raised in a land of battle,
If you clash with those of another faith,
If you fight with enemies,
If you load steel shot by the pood,
If you pile on great loads of dried provisions,
He will never toss his neck.
If great trouble falls upon you,
He lacks only a tongue to speak:
Zhelmaian is wiser than other beasts.
When you say, 'Go!' the creature,
As though about to fly away,
Begins his work like a whirlwind.
Stretching his long, sprawling legs,
All the roads of the world
He leaves behind before an eye can open.
This creature Zhelmaian
Is both a champion and a mighty camel;
This dark camel standing here
Will be of great use to you, Manas.
My champion, your lion's courage
I prized and knew with longing.
With my own hands, Zhelmaian,
As a trust for the greathearted one,
I had wished to give.
I have set right what went wrong for you;
Giving Zhelmaian into your hands,
My accomplished one, I have supported you.
Spoken of by men, yet beyond their sight,
I am your Shai Ata himself;
Of one who will support you,
I am the watching dark eye!
You have gathered every champion for your need.
The dark camel with a broad hump,
Khan Manas's Zhelmaian,
With my own hands I entrust to you;
Today I give him as a gift!
Zhelmaian, a faithful companion among beasts,
Take him as your faithful companion.
